CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up of chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient with chronic congestive heart failure with diastolic dysfunction presenting for follow-up prior to scheduled right knee replacement surgery. She had an exacerbation of heart failure in the spring with increasing dyspnea. Furosemide was switched to torsemide 20 mg daily and lisinopril was increased to 10 mg daily in March. BNP was 3,000 in March and increased to 6,000 in April. Since medication adjustments, patient reports weight loss of approximately 3-3.5 pounds and significantly improved urinary urgency. She currently denies dyspnea. She is not on potassium supplementation. Patient reports an episode of bilateral leg cramps which she attributed to sleeping with ceiling fan on, relieved by pickle juice (4 ounces). Regarding heartburn, she reports it was problematic at one point, took prilosec for approximately 2 weeks in January, then switched to another stomach medication with no further issues. She has right knee replacement surgery scheduled for June 24. She is interested in scheduling a colonoscopy prior to anticipated insurance coverage changes.
